constraints: GATE: in autornd/evals/cli.py, before the first scenario and before any client call, run preflight.run(). If any finding is not ok, print every finding, make no paid call, and exit with a distinct non-zero code.

OVERRIDE: --skip-preflight is allowed. The results header then records preflight {ran: false, override: true}. When the gate runs, the header records every finding (ok, name, detail), so the record shows what was verified before the spend.

NEW CHECK: for each pinned tier (model plus provider pin), the endpoint the pin selects must list, in supported_parameters, every parameter the harness sends on that tier: at least response_format and max_tokens. Derive the sent set from the client's payload construction, or guard a hand list with a test that builds a real payload and compares. A listing with no supported_parameters field is BLIND: report it as not ok, with that word, because no evidence must never be reported as no problem (convention 28). An unpinned tier is reported as 'unpinned — parameter support depends on the router's choice' and does not fail.

TESTS (provider-free, through the real gate function or cli main, with the catalogue fetch mocked): (a) a failing finding refuses the sweep with zero billed client calls; (b) all ok, so it proceeds; (c) --skip-preflight proceeds and the header records the override; (d) a pinned endpoint lacking response_format gives a failing finding naming tier, model and pin; (e) a listing without supported_parameters gives a blind finding; (f) the header carries the findings, read back from disk. PROVE BY BREAKING: make the gate ignore findings and show (a) fail.
Free. No model name in code. No change to any pin.
